releases.body: Remove duplicate workspace.manage command that conflicted with built-in /workspaces slash command.

releases.name: v0.2.0 — Lean on built-in workspace UI
releases.body:
## v0.2.0

### Breaking change
Requires `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_WORKSPACES=1` (or `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL=1`). The plugin now delegates workspace list, create, delete, and reset to OpenCode's built-in UI and focuses on the UX gaps it fills uniquely.

### What's removed (now handled by built-in)
- Toggle enable/disable (`command.workspace.toggle` is built-in)
- Delete workspace dialog (built-in `/workspaces` has better UX with unmerged-change detection)
- Reset workspace dialog (built-in handles session archiving)
- Sidebar workspace list (`sidebar_content` slot — built-in renders its own list)
- Worktree API fallback and synthetic workspace fabrication

### What's kept (plugin-unique)
- Switch workspace dialog with status indicators
- Rename workspace (KV-persisted display names)
- Home dashboard card (`home_bottom` slot)
- Prompt badge showing current workspace (`home_prompt_right` slot)
- Sidebar footer actions: + new / ⎇ switch / ≡ manage
- Full manage route (`/workspaces`)
- Slash commands: `/ws`, `/ws-new`, `/ws-switch`, `/ws-sessions`, `/wsm`, `/wsc`, `/wsl`
- Session browser grouped by workspace

### What's new
- `createWorkspace()` now calls `experimental.workspace.create()` directly (was using `worktree.create()`)

Fix npm plugin loading: use actual .ts/.tsx extensions in imports

OpenCode's bun-plugin-solid calls readFileSync() on import paths during analysis. The TypeScript ESM convention of using .js extensions (e.g. './components.js') was causing ENOENT errors since the actual files are .tsx/.ts. This was the root cause of the silent plugin load failure when installed from npm.

Fix: Add @jsxImportSource pragma to all JSX source files.

Without the per-file JSX pragma, Bun cannot determine the JSX transform when loading source files from the npm cache (no tsconfig.json is available in the installed package). This caused the plugin to silently fail when configured as an npm plugin.

The fix matches the pattern used by oc-plugin-rainbow and other working TUI plugins.

Fix: mark tui peer deps as required so npm installs solid-js and @opentui

Root cause: @opentui/solid, @opentui/core and solid-js were marked as optional peer deps, causing npm to skip them during installation. Without these packages, the Bun JSX transform plugin and solid-js cannot be resolved at runtime, silently preventing the TUI plugin from loading.

Fix: Only @opencode-ai/plugin remains optional (it's provided by the OpenCode host). The three TUI framework packages are now required peer deps and will be installed automatically.
